Lacy's *Gemini Rights* was released July 15 (2022) and was his sophomore album and first on RCA. The breakup is central to it. Lacy has described the record as being about finding himself after a heartbreak, and he framed it as hopeful rather than sad. To me, the subject matter could be sad if you look at it that way, but I feel like it is way more hopeful — and that's the story: finding happiness.

- Songfacts reports that Lacy split in November 2021 from a boyfriend of seven months, and that the couple tried to get back together but it didn't work. He told The Guardian he kept trying, and nothing was working.

- Lacy told AOL/Billboard-style coverage that the anger was fueled by specific betrayals, including finding his handmade ceramics at his ex's place and learning the ex had lunch with his younger sister to discuss the breakup.
- Lacy said his ex liked the album, though some lines made him pause.

On the creative process, Lacy's Apple Music artist statement says that realizing he isn't separate from his audience made the album feel very easy and fun to make. **Background and release**
- Lacy signed to RCA Records in 2021. He first recorded "Bad Habit" in June 2021, using a beat he made with drums he'd used before. He called writing it a turning point, saying it was "the start of this renaissance of the separation between [past] Steve and [present] Steve." ([GQ, Jeremy Gordon, June 23, 2022](https://www.gq.com/story/gq-hype-steve-lacy))
- After Fousheé heard the instrumental, the two freestyled over it for about 20 minutes, which led to verses and a chorus melody. Lacy later changed the breakdown, drums, and chorus. ([The Guardian, Shaad D'Souza, Dec. 22, 2022](https://www.theguardian.com/music/2022/dec/22/my-mom-thinks-im-doing-drugs-but-im-at-home-baking-cookies-steve-lacy-on-his-breakout-year))
- Lacy said the song was finished a week before he submitted *Gemini Rights* to RCA (same Guardian source).
- It was released June 29, 2022, as the second single from *Gemini Rights* (released July 15, 2022).
- Fan-made sped-up versions went viral on TikTok. RCA later released an official sped-up version, which Lacy initially found "gross" but eventually agreed to (Guardian source above).

**Composition**
- The page describes the track as psychedelic, lo-fi, R&B, bedroom pop, and alt-pop ballad, with many other influences listed.
- Sheet music shows F minor, 84–88 BPM, with vocals from C4 to C6 (cited to Musicnotes). Lacy sings mostly in falsetto.
- The song opens with Fousheé's vocals and has three parts, ending in a stripped-back a cappella section and a "chaotic" jazz fusion breakdown (Los Angeles Times, Aug Brown, Oct. 10, 2022).
- The main instrument is a slightly warped guitar riff, which Paul Tingen says Pogue mixed as the song's main focus (Sound on Sound, Dec. 2022).
- The chorus was changed after a suggestion from Tyler, the Creator, who felt the revised line would "be more memorable" (Billboard Chartbreaker interview, Aug. 3, 2022, [link](https://www.billboard.com/music/features/steve-lacy-bad-habit-billboard-august-2022-chartbreaker-interview-1235121728/)).
- Lacy described the lyrics as "a play on confidence," moving from feeling unworthy to feeling "almost too good" but "still down" (Guardian source above).
- Lacy said the a cappella section was meant to sound like he was "singing directly to" the listener (GQ source above).
- Lacy later told Rolling Stone that the refrain reflected fans wanting something from him that he didn't know about ([Rolling Stone, Jeff Ihaza, Oct. 20, 2022](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/steve-lacy-bad-habit-grammy-preview-1234607474/)).

**Writers and producers**
- Writers (per the page's credits): Steve Lacy, Diana Gordon (wrote part of the ending), John Carroll Kirby, Britanny/Brittany Fousheé (the page uses both spellings), and Matthew Castellanos.
- Producer: Steve Lacy. Lacy also played bass and handled songwriting.
- Kirby is credited with additional synths.

**C6. Bad Habit의 제작 경과** [보도·재인용(Wikipedia 경유, 원문 미열람)]
- 2021년 6월에 시작했습니다(GQ).
- Fousheé와 약 20분 즉흥으로 부른 뒤 Lacy가 브레이크다운, 드럼, 후렴을 고쳤습니다. 앨범을 RCA에 넘기기 일주일 전에 완성했습니다(Guardian).
- Tyler, the Creator의 제안으로 후렴을 바꿨습니다(Billboard).
- 모두 원문을 확인하지 못했습니다[S8].
- 믹서 Neal Pogue의 설명은 원문으로 확인했습니다 [직접 발언·원문 확인][S9]: "The focus of 'Bad Habit' is the main guitar, and everything else supports that." 이는 믹서의 작업 의도이지 청취 결과가 아닙니다.

**C7. 크레딧 역할이 출처마다 다름** [DB등재·상충]
- Genius에서는 John Carroll Kirby가 프로듀서 6/9트랙, Ely Rise가 프로듀서 5/9트랙입니다. Wikipedia 인원 목록에서 두 사람은 연주자로만 나옵니다.
  - Kirby: 3번 오르간, 5–10번 신시사이저
  - Rise: 1–4번 건반·피아노·신시사이저
- 작곡 크레딧도 다릅니다. Genius 집계는 Kirby 6/9, Rise 5/9입니다. Wikipedia 기준으로는 Kirby가 1, 5, 6번, Rise가 3, 4, 10번입니다.
- Dahi(Wikipedia 표기 Dacoury Natche): Genius는 3, 4, 10번 프로듀서로 등재합니다. Wikipedia는 4, 10번 공동 프로듀싱과 3번 기타(misc.) 프로듀싱으로 구분합니다.
- Matt Martians의 3, 4번 기타 프로듀싱은 Wikipedia에만 있습니다.
- Yuli의 10번 작곡 크레딧은 Genius에만 있습니다.
- 부클릿이나 유통 크레딧은 확보하지 못했습니다. **이 상충이 해결되기 전까지 Kirby·Rise의 '프로듀서' 역할을 핵심 논거로 쓰지 마십시오.**

**C8. 샘플** [DB등재·상충/미확인]
- **2Gether (Enterlude)**: Genius는 "C418 — Mellohi 샘플"로 등재합니다. WhoSampled 검색 결과 제목에서는 2Gether와 Mellohi가 모두 Mellotron "SlowWaltz"를 샘플링한 것으로 보입니다[검색 결과 경유]. 따라서 **공통 원천 음원**일 가능성이 있으며, 마인크래프트 곡을 직접 인용했다고 확정할 수 없습니다.
- **Mercury**: Eddie Kendricks "Just Memories" 샘플은 Genius 단일 등재입니다. 두 차례 검색에서 이를 뒷받침하는 자료를 찾지 못해 해당 가지를 중단했습니다[DB등재·미확인]. 확인 경로는 ④에 둡니다.
- 무크레딧 인용 보고는 이번 조사에서 찾지 못했습니다.
